premise.claim: Every RBG admission webhook has failurePolicy: Fail, so every RoleBasedGroup create or update depends on at least one of the two controller replicas being reachable; neither the Helm chart nor config/ ships a PodDisruptionBudget or replica spreading, so draining a node can evict both replicas at once.
premise.evidence: All 6 webhook configurations carry failurePolicy: Fail (config/webhook/manifests.yaml and deploy/helm/rbgs/templates/webhook/manifests.yaml); the PR's three chart tests fail on base 1fc69f70 with 'PodDisruptionBudget rbgs-controller-manager not found' (results/chart-tests-base.out) and pass on the head (results/chart-tests-head.out).

findings.note: Acceptance contract: both install paths ship the PDB (maxUnavailable: 1, AlwaysAllow, selector matches manager pods) and the hostname ScheduleAnyway spread; opt-outs (enabled=false, constraints=[]) work. PR's own tests; fail on base, pass on head.

Eviction semantics of the shipped PDB object against a real API server: Ready pod refused at DisruptionsAllowed=0 (429), evicted at 1 (decremented), unready pod evicted at 0 only because of AlwaysAllow (IfHealthyBudget control refuses).

liveNote: L3 not run (no cluster in this round): a real kubectl drain of a node running one manager replica should evict exactly that one pod while the other keeps serving the webhooks; on a single-node cluster the drain is expected to block on the second replica until a replacement is Ready (standard PDB behavior).
